question: Three resistances of 8Ω, 12Ω and 24Ω are connected in parallel. The resistance of this combination will be □( ).
solution:
The correct answer is __**4 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The three resistances given are 8Ω, 12Ω, and 24Ω.
 
• These resistances are connected in parallel.
 
• The formula to calculate the equivalent resistance (Rₑq) for parallel resistances is: 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃.
 
• Substituting the given resistances into the formula gives us the equivalent resistance of 4Ω.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance:**

 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor.
 
• The unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω).
 
• Resistors are used in electrical circuits to control the flow of current.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Connection:**
 
 
• In a parallel connection, the resistors are connected across the same two points, providing multiple paths for the current to flow.
 
• The voltage across each resistor in a parallel circuit is the same.
 
• The total or equivalent resistance of resistors in parallel is always less than the smallest individual resistor in the network.
 
 
 
• **Calculating Equivalent Resistance in Parallel:**
 
 
• When resistors are connected in parallel, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances.
 
• The formula is: 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃...
 
• For the given resistances, 1/Rₑq = 1/8 + 1/12 + 1/24. Simplifying this gives us 1/Rₑq = 1/4, so Rₑq = 4Ω.
